account: Scientists at the European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts (ECMWF) set up Pangu-Weather, a machine-learning model that Huawei Cloud trained on ERA5 reanalysis data, on ECMWF computers. They started it from the same operational analyses as ECMWF's physics-based Integrated Forecasting System (IFS) and compared ten-day forecasts, mainly for the year from 1 March 2022 to 28 February 2023, with 2018 used for tropical cyclones. The authors report that accuracy was comparable for global scores and for extreme events, checked against IFS analyses and against station observations. For 2-meter temperature events over Europe in summer, Pangu-Weather discriminated events better than the IFS, with significant differences for thresholds between the 75th and 90th percentiles; in winter the two models performed alike. Differences in tropical cyclone track error were small and not significant. The authors also report weaknesses. The forecasts are too smooth, bias grows with lead time, and cyclone intensity is forecast poorly. The Bulletin of the American Meteorological Society published the study on 6 June 2024. The authors evaluated deterministic forecasts from one model and did not measure any use in warnings.
